q: Over an average lifetime, roughly how many times does a human heart beat?
w: ~70 beats per minute × ~79 years ≈ 2.9 billion; the commonly cited figure is 2.5–3 billion. Your heart is startlingly industrious.

q: Roughly how many piano tuners work in New York City?
w: The original Fermi estimate: NYC has ~8M people, maybe 100k pianos, tuned ~1–2× a year, each tuner doing 4–6 a day — you land around 100–200.

q: Counting all its branches, roughly how long is the Great Wall of China in kilometers?
w: A 2008 government survey of all dynasties’ sections put it at 21,196 km. The Ming-era stonework most people picture is about 8,850 km.

q: Roughly how many hairs grow on the average human head?
w: About 100,000, with blondes averaging more (~140k) and redheads fewer (~90k). Each lasts ~3 years before falling out.

q: Roughly how many cups of coffee are drunk worldwide on an average day?
w: ~2.25 billion cups a day — roughly one cup for every 3–4 humans alive, before breakfast even ends.

q: Roughly how many registered motor vehicles are there in the United States?
w: About 280 million registered vehicles — comfortably more than one per American adult. The US has been a carapaced nation since the 1970s.

q: Roughly how many books are held in the US Library of Congress?
w: ~25 million books (cataloged) out of ~170 million total items including maps, films, and recordings. The largest library on Earth.

q: What is the total weight of the Eiffel Tower, in metric tonnes?
w: About 10,100 tonnes of wrought iron — 7,300 t of it in the lattice structure alone, plus paint, elevators, and restaurants.

q: What is the mass of the International Space Station, in kilograms?
w: ~420,000 kg — a football-field-sized outpost assembled over 40+ missions and continuously crewed since November 2000.

q: At its peak around 100 CE, roughly how many people lived in the city of Rome itself?
w: Around one million — the first city in history to reach that mark. Estimates range from 800k to over a million depending on who counts as a resident.

q: Roughly how many steps would it take to walk around the Earth at the equator?
w: 40,075 km at ~0.75 m per stride ≈ 53 million steps. Water walking not included.

q: How many liters of water does an Olympic swimming pool hold?
w: 2,500 m³ = 2.5 million liters (2.5 megaliters). The standard spec: 50 m × 25 m × ~2 m deep on average.

q: Roughly how many Google searches are performed worldwide each day?
w: Commonly cited at ~8.5 billion a day — nearly one per person alive, daily. (Search is the water we swim in.)

q: Roughly how many chickens are alive on Earth at any given moment?
w: ~25 billion. Chickens are the most numerous bird in history by a wild margin — there are roughly 3 chickens per human.

q: Roughly how much gold has been mined in all of human history, in metric tonnes?
w: About 210,000 t — which would fit in a cube ~22 meters on a side. Nearly all of it mined in the last century and a half.

q: Roughly how many total words did William Shakespeare write across all his works?
w: ~884,000 words across 37+ plays and 154 sonnets — and he introduced or popularized hundreds of words still in daily use.

q: Roughly how many photographs are taken worldwide each year?
w: Estimates run to ~2 trillion a year — about half of them by smartphones, and overwhelmingly selfies adjacent to food.

q: Roughly how many babies are born worldwide on an average day?
w: ~365,000 per day — about 4 every second, which works out to ~132 million a year.

q: The Moon’s distance from Earth is about how many Earth diameters?
w: ~30 Earths would fit side by side between us and the Moon (384,400 km ÷ 12,742 km ≈ 30). It’s much farther than most diagrams suggest.

q: Roughly how many solar eclipses (total or partial) occur somewhere on Earth per century?
w: About 240 per century — roughly 2–5 per year somewhere on the planet, though any single spot waits ~375 years for a total eclipse.

q: Roughly how many pizzas are sold in the United States per year?
w: ~3 billion a year — about 350 slices per second. Americans eat roughly 23 pounds of pizza per person annually.

q: Roughly how many liters of water does Lake Superior contain?
w: ~12,100 km³ = about 1.2 × 10¹⁶ liters — enough to cover North and South America in a foot of water. It holds 10% of the world’s surface freshwater.
